title: Surge-buffered leaky-integrator scaling policy for throughput SLAs
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Problem: Dedicated customers require firm throughput guarantees and graceful handling of sudden spikes (surges) without violating latency SLOs or exhausting GPU pools. Current autoscaling strategies respond either too aggressively (cost blowouts) or too conservatively (missed SLAs) under bursty traffic patterns that are common for chat/LLM workloads.

Proposal summary: Implement a surge-buffered, leaky-integrator scaling controller that blends short-term surge headroom with a smoothed long-term demand signal. The controller uses a proportional-multiplier compute for immediate corrective action, a leaky integrator for bounded accumulation of load pressure, and a fixed surge reservoir to absorb short spikes without immediate scale-out. Safety limits clamp scale decisions to tenant and fleet-level caps and apply staged ramping to avoid oscillation.

Key design points:
- Target metrics: combined view of observed token throughput (tokens/s), request queue depth, and serving latency percentiles (p50/p95). Primary control signal is token throughput relative to per-tenant reserved throughput target; latency is used as a guardrail.
- Algorithm: 1) Compute short_term_load = max(current_tokens_per_s / target_tokens_per_s, queue_depth_normalized) 2) Compute integral = leaky_integrator.integrate(short_term_load, decay=60s) 3) Desired_multiplier = base_multiplier * (1 + alpha * (short_term_load - 1)) + beta * integral 4) If short_term_load <= 1 + surge_threshold, consume surge_reservoir (atomic) and defer scale-out. 5) Apply staged ramp: scale_change = clamp(previous_scale * Desired_multiplier, min_step, max_step) 6) Enforce cooldown windows and jitter to reduce synchronized actions across tenants.
- Surge reservoir: per-tenant soft headroom (configurable, default 20% of committed capacity) that allows short bursts to be absorbed. The reservoir recharges slowly during low utilization periods. Reservoir usage is exposed in telemetry and can trigger billing/alerts if repeatedly consumed.
- Safety limits: absolute max_scale (percent over commit), min_idle_capacity floor, per-tenant QPS/token caps, global fleet safety budget, and emergency fallback policy that routes traffic to hosted fallback model variants when limits are hit.
- Sequence/trace awareness: when a request sequence (chat session) is in progress, scaling decisions give priority to preserving KV cache affinity (avoid evicting nodes hosting active sessions). A node eviction score includes active_sequence_weight to reduce disruption to in-progress requests.

Why this is different: Rather than pure threshold-based scaling or ML-predicted scaling, this approach combines a control-theory style integrator with a discrete surge buffer and explicit safety envelopes tuned for LLM workload characteristics (bursty requests, long token streams, cache affinity). It aims to reduce cost while meeting throughput SLAs and minimizing user-visible latency degradation during spikes.
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes desired scale every 10s and respects per-tenant max_scale cap
Short bursts up to configured surge_reservoir are absorbed without triggering scale-out
P95 latency for canary tenants does not increase > 15% under a 3x synthetic burst compared to baseline
Scale oscillations are reduced vs current baseline (measured as < 5 scale events per hour for synthetic workload)
Telemetry emits metrics: desired_multiplier, integral_value, reservoir_level, scale_decision_reason
Canary rollout to 3 dedicated customers with manual rollback capability succeeds for 48h without SLA violations
implementation_notes: Controller implemented as pluggable policy in scaling-orchestrator module (runtime/executor)
Add config knobs: alpha, beta, decay_seconds, surge_threshold, surge_reservoir_pct, min_step, max_step, cooldown_seconds
Unit tests: deterministic integrator tests, reservoir exhaustion scenarios, clamp/enforcement tests
Integration tests: replay synthetic spike traces and measure scale decisions and latency on staging cluster
Avoid global clock sync assumptions; use monotonic timers and include jitter for multi-tenant coordination
rollout_plan: 1) Dev: feature branch + unit tests (2 weeks)
2) Staging: integration tests + canary simulation (1 week)
3) Canary: enable policy for 3 low-risk dedicated customers with telemetry and escalation on-call (2 weeks)
4) Gradual ramp: expand canary coverage by 10 tenants every 48h if error budgets and cost delta acceptable
5) GA: enable policy by default for new dedicated allocations and opt-in for existing customers after review
comments: 2026-02-03 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached in Confluence. Agreed to prioritize reservoir size and recharge behaviour as tuning knobs.
2026-02-14 - Marco Reyes: PoC of leaky integrator implemented; basic unit tests green. Observed that decay=30s is too aggressive with long token streams.
2026-02-20 - Sophia Kim (PM): Requested explicit billing/alerting behaviour when reservoir usage > 50% for 10m. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-01 - Dev Lead (Ethan Moore): Raised concern about cross-tenant correlated scaling during region-wide traffic spikes; added global fleet safety budget and jitter.
2026-03-10 - Security Review (Anita Rao): No immediate security blockers. Ensure metrics do not leak tenant identifiers in shared dashboards.
2026-03-12 - Marco Reyes: Candidate rollout plan ready; PRs opened for infra and runtime. Staging replay shows 40% reduction in immediate scale-outs for bursty traces.
